shellToolCall.description: Build app to verify view transitions compile

events.content:
View transitions are wired up across the gallery using React’s `<ViewTransition>` and Next.js `transitionTypes` on links.

### Shared element morph (grid → detail)
Product thumbnails and hero images share a `ViewTransition` name (`product-{slug}`) with `share="morph"`, so the browser morphs the image from its grid cell to the detail layout.

### Directional page slides
- Product cards use `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}` when navigating to detail
- The back link uses `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`
- Both pages wrap content in a `PageTransition` component that maps those types to slide-left / slide-right animations

### Suspense skeleton reveals
Skeleton fallbacks exit with `slide-down`; resolved content enters with `slide-up`, with staggered timing so the skeleton clears before content appears. This is active on the product detail page (async `ProductDetails`) and ready on the home page grid.

### Reduced motion
A `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query disables all view-transition animations and skeleton pulse effects.

### Files changed
- `app/PageTransition.tsx` — reusable directional page wrapper
- `app/ProductGrid.tsx` — shared element names + forward navigation type
- `app/page.tsx` — page transitions + Suspense reveal wrappers
- `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` — morphing hero, back navigation, Suspense reveal
- `app/globals.css` — morph, slide, reveal, and reduced-motion styles
- `react-canary.d.ts` — TypeScript types for `ViewTransition`

Run `npm run dev` and click a product card to see the image morph and page slide forward; use “Back to products” to slide back. On the detail page, the text skeleton should smoothly hand off to the loaded content.
